scenarios.name: single filer, Massachusetts state contributory pension: fully exempt under MA law, engine taxes it in full
scenarios.source: mass.gov 'Tax Treatment of Government Pensions in Massachusetts', section 'Massachusetts state and local employee contributory pension': 'Massachusetts state/local employee pensions are contributory annuity, pension, endowment, or retirement funds of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts (or any of its political subdivisions)...Distributions made to you from a Massachusetts state and local employee contributory plan are excluded from Massachusetts gross income even though they are included in federal gross income.' No age gate is stated for this exclusion. LABEL CORRECTED IN PHASE 5b TASK 4: this row read 'otherStateOrLocal' only because the PlanSource enum had no case for the taxpayer's OWN state system when the fixture was written. Task 1 added 'ownStateOrLocal', which is what a Commonwealth of Massachusetts contributory pension is to a Massachusetts resident, and this row now carries it. The old label was the same mislabel Kansas carried and was dangerous rather than merely imprecise: 'otherStateOrLocal' means a DIFFERENT state's system, its entire reason for existing is to stop an out-of-state pension claiming a state's own exclusion, and a Massachusetts rule naming it would have exempted a California public pension held by a Massachusetts resident. WHAT THE SHIPPED RULE CANNOT SEE, and what this row therefore cannot prove: the Massachusetts exclusion is conditioned on the plan being CONTRIBUTORY, and RetirementPlanClassification has no contributory axis, so this row is indistinguishable from a noncontributory Massachusetts municipal pension, which is taxable. That is recorded as a known-but-unpinned defect in GoldenScenarioDefectCatalogueTests.knownButUnpinned, and it is why a golden case for the noncontributory household was deliberately NOT written: it would carry inputs identical to this one and a contradictory expectedStateTax. Arithmetic: $60,000 fully excluded, $0 state taxable income (MA's stateDeduction is 'none' in this app's config, so there is no separate standard deduction to apply), tax = $0.00.

scenarios.name: UNESTABLISHED-JURISDICTION GUARD, do not simplify away: single filer, a government pension whose employing jurisdiction was never established, fully taxable -- the case that proves a Massachusetts rule exempting ownStateOrLocal does NOT also exempt governmentUnspecified
scenarios.source: mass.gov 'Tax Treatment of Government Pensions in Massachusetts' enumerates a closed list of exempt pension categories (MA/local contributory, federal contributory, MBTA, out-of-state reciprocal contributory, railroad retirement, U.S. uniformed-services noncontributory). A government pension whose employing jurisdiction was never established matches none of those named categories, so by the closed-list structure of this guidance it remains ordinary taxable pension income under M.G.L. c. 62 (an inference from the enumeration's closed-list structure, not a sentence stating it verbatim on the page). WHAT THIS ROW ACTUALLY ENCODES, corrected in Phase 5b Task 4: 'governmentUnspecified' means 'a government employer whose jurisdiction was not established', per that case's own doc comment, which forbids any rule treating it as a specific jurisdiction. It does NOT mean 'noncontributory'. This case was previously named and described as the noncontributory municipal pension, and it cannot be that: no field on this row distinguishes contributory from noncontributory, so it would have passed identically whether the shipped rule respected that distinction or ignored it. It is a real and load-bearing guard, in the same role as Kansas's KS-8, and it is now named for the thing it actually proves. The noncontributory-municipal household is NOT expressible in this app's model and is recorded in GoldenScenarioDefectCatalogueTests.knownButUnpinned instead. Arithmetic: $60,000 fully taxable at the flat 5% rate = $3,000.00.

scenarios.name: MFJ, both spouses have MA state/local contributory pensions: fully exempt under MA law, engine taxes the full household income
scenarios.source: mass.gov 'Tax Treatment of Government Pensions in Massachusetts', section 'Massachusetts state and local employee contributory pension' (see single-filer case above for the exact quote). No per-taxpayer cap is stated -- distributions are excluded outright regardless of amount. LABEL CORRECTED IN PHASE 5b TASK 4: both rows here read 'otherStateOrLocal' for what are Commonwealth of Massachusetts systems, i.e. the taxpayer's OWN state, and both now carry 'ownStateOrLocal' (added by Task 1). See the single-filer case above for why the old label was dangerous rather than merely imprecise, and for the contributory-axis limitation this row shares with it. Arithmetic: $40,000 + $35,000 = $75,000, all fully excluded, $0 state taxable income, tax = $0.00.

scenarios.name: MFJ, one spouse's U.S. uniformed-services pension is exempt and the other spouse's private 401(k) distribution is not: one spouse qualifies
scenarios.source: mass.gov 'Tax Treatment of Government Pensions in Massachusetts', section 'U.S. military non-contributory pension': 'U.S. military pensions, which are included in federal gross income, are excluded from Massachusetts gross income.' LABEL CORRECTED IN PHASE 5b TASK 4: this row read 'federalCivilian' only because the PlanSource enum had no distinct case for U.S. uniformed-services retired pay when the fixture was written. Task 1 added 'uniformedServices' and this row now carries it. The military exclusion is deliberately NOT written against 'federalCivilian': mass.gov's guidance exempts U.S. military pensions, and separately treats federal CIVILIAN (CSRS/FERS) pensions under a different heading, so a rule naming 'federalCivilian' would over-exempt. The shipped Massachusetts rule names 'uniformedServices' and 'ownStateOrLocal' only, and 'federalCivilian' is deliberately absent; see the Task 4 report for the disclosed under-match that leaves. The private 401(k) distribution is ordinary taxable pension/annuity income with no MA exclusion. Arithmetic: $30,000 military fully excluded; $30,000 private taxable; $30,000 x 5% = $1,500.00.
